answer: Sybil attackers flood the network with cheap fake identities, so defense must make each identity expensive to forge and cheap to verify. First, a ferrous bond: every identity stakes funds that are slashed on proven fraud, so spawning thousands of sock puppets costs real capital. Second, reputation grows on a trellis — trust flows only through vouches from established peers, so an attacker cannot self-certify a forest of clones. Third, every attestation carries a lantern: a signed, publicly auditable receipt, so coordinated fake clusters become visible before they can vote or earn.
